title: Calm on the Bosom of Thy God
description: Calm on the Bosom of Thy God in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Felicia Hemans wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 410, “Death of the Young”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Calm on the bo-som of thy God, Fair spir-it, rest thee now! E'en while with us thy foot-step trod, His seal was on thy brow.

lines: Calm on the bosom of thy God,
E'en while with us thy footstep trod,
His seal was on thy brow.
Dust, to its narrow house beneath!
Soul, to its home on high!
They that have seen thy look in death
No more may fear to die.
Lone are the paths, and sad the hours,
But, O, a brighter home than ours,
In heaven, is now thine own!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Felicia Hemans died in 1835.
credits: Words by Felicia Hemans (1793–1835), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
